svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "Quorum sensing: bacteria count themselves by chemical signals."], [1, "Each Vibrio fischeri cell releases a little autoinducer."], [3, "When cells are few, it diffuses away: too dilute to have an effect."], [6, "As the cells multiply, the autoinducer builds up past a threshold..."], [8.5, "...binds the LuxR receptor and switches on the lux genes: the population glows together."], [11.5, "In the bobtail squid, the glowing bacteria hide its shadow on moonlit nights."]]
svg.title: Quorum sensing
svg.desc: Quorum sensing in Vibrio fischeri: autoinducer released by each cell stays dilute at low density but passes a threshold at high density, activating luciferase so the population glows; the bacteria give the bobtail squid counter-illumination.

g.data-info: The autoinducer diffuses away and stays dilute: no light.
A small signal molecule (an acyl-homoserine lactone) made by every cell by the enzyme LuxI. It diffuses in and out of cells.
The autoinducer builds up above a threshold. It binds the receptor LuxR, which switches on the lux genes.

svg.text: Autoinducer and light vs cell density

g.data-info: Luciferase makes light. More LuxI is made too: positive feedback, so the whole population switches on together.

g.text: Inside one cell at high density
LuxI is also made → more autoinducer: positive feedback

g.data-info: Its light organ holds a dense culture of Vibrio fischeri. The light, shining down, matches moonlight and hides the squid's shadow from predators below (counter-illumination).

g.text: bobtail squid: light organ glows down
no shadow seen by predators below

g.data-info: At dawn the squid expels most of the bacteria; the rest multiply during the day, so by night the density is high again.
